The heredoc was too long and got truncated. I'll write the spec in small chunks.

{"action":"shell","command":"cat > /testbed/specs/001-transactions/spec.md <<'EOF'
# Feature Specification: Batch Journal Writer for TinyDB

**Feature Branch**: `001-transactions`

**Created**: 2026-10-17 | **Last Updated**: 2026-10-17

**Status**: Draft (milestone 3 supersedes milestone 1/2 text where conflicting)

**Input**: User description: "Build tinydb.journal.BatchWriter(db) wrapping a supplied TinyDB instance without changing its ordinary APIs, default table only. R01 apply(operations) accepts a list of operation dicts (insert document / remove by positive integer doc_id), returns inserted IDs, [] for empty input, ValueError for unknown/malformed operations. R02 atomic batch: validate and apply sequentially, on any error restore the complete pre-batch default-table data; missing-ID remove is an error; previously acquired default-table handles reflect success and rollback. R03 ordinary TinyDB reads/writes and preexisting documents keep working; inserted and returned nested data must not alias caller input; mutating an operation after apply cannot mutate the database. R04 reject bool as doc_id; validate structurally before committing; ValueError for unsupported fields, non-list operations, or non-dict documents; accept empty dict documents. R05 preview(operations) returns the inserted IDs apply would produce, leaving all data and the next insertion ID unchanged including on errors; preview and failed apply must not consume IDs; existing table handles and query caches stay coherent. R06 direct db.insert between calls must be seen by the wrapper; no stale initial snapshot. R05b preview returns a new detached list on every call; mutating a previously returned preview list affects neither later previews nor internal state. R05 clarification: apply advances the wrapper's next-insertion-ID state on every successful batch and writes it back to the underlying table so subsequent inserts (apply or direct db.insert) continue the sequence without reuse or rewind, even across removes. R07 apply(operations, token=None) supports an optional nonempty string idempotency token: repeating an already successful identical batch/token returns a detached copy of the original inserted IDs without rerunning mutations, even after other direct writes; reusing a token with different operations raises ValueError without changing data; failed batches do not consume a token; None means normal operation; invalid tokens raise ValueError. R08 token bookkeeping belongs to this BatchWriter instance, never in user documents; preview never records/consumes a token and keeps its original signature; return lists must not expose internal token bookkeeping through mutation."
EOF
echo OK1"}
